title: Claudia Sheinbaum’s Cry at the Zócalo Drew More Than 300,000 Attendees: Mexico City Authorities
author: Kevin Ruiz
content:
_This article by[Kevin Ruiz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Kevin%20Ruiz)
originally appeared in the [September 15, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/15/capital/grito-de-
claudia-sheinbaum-en-el-zocalo-registro-mas-de-300-mil-asistentes-secgob),
Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. The Mexico City Government Secretariat (SECGOB) reported that
the celebration for the 216th anniversary of Mexico's Independence, led by
President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, drew a turnout of **more than 300,000
attendees**. In an informational note, they stated that the activities
unfolded peacefully and **concluded with a clean record and no incidents**.
People's participation, they noted, was orderly, "which made it possible to
guarantee safe conditions."

They specified that there was support from thousands of people for President
Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who came to the Zocalo to take part in the occasion.

![Aerial view of the packed Zócalo during the Cry of
Independence](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/zocalo-300000-aerial.jpg)Photo: Yazmin Ortega Cortes

## The Celebration Extended to the Boroughs

The capital's various boroughs gathered thousands of people in their main
squares to witness the Cry of Independence delivered by the heads of each
borough, as well as the celebrations afterward.

In Cuauhtemoc, 10,000 people gathered to see groups such as Los Chicos N5,
Matute, and Luis Ángel El Flaco. In Azcapotzalco, official figures indicate
15,000 people gathered on the borough's esplanade.

As for the Coyoacan borough, authorities recorded the entry and exit of **a
little over 100,000 visitors** throughout September 15. Meanwhile, at the time
of the Cry of Independence, 28,000 remained in the main square.
